content: Tigecycline is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, particularly when other antibiotics have proven ineffective. It belongs to the glycylcycline class of antibiotics, which are structurally related to tetracyclines. Tigecycline works by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis. It binds to the 30S ribosomal subunit, preventing the entry of aminoacyl-tRNA molecules into the ribosome's A site, thereby halting bacterial growth. This medication is administered intravenously over 30 to 60 minutes by a healthcare professional, typically every 12 hours as directed by a physician. If you are preparing or using this medication at home, ensure you have been properly instructed by a healthcare provider. The medication should be gently swirled to mix; do not shake it. The reconstituted solution should appear yellow to orange in color. Before use, inspect the solution for particles or discoloration (green or black); if present, do not use the product. Tigecycline is only effective against bacterial infections and will not treat viral infections such as the common cold or flu. For optimal results, it is important to use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and to complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, and pain or swelling at the injection site. Rarely, tigecycline and other tetracycline-class drugs may cause increased intracranial pressure (intracranial hypertension, or IH), which is more likely in overweight women of childbearing age or those with a history of IH. While IH typically resolves after discontinuing tigecycline, there is a risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. Additionally, tigecycline may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile) infection, which can occur during or even weeks to months after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Tigecycline may increase sensitivity to sunlight. Limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Children under 8 years of age may be more susceptible to side effects, particularly tooth discoloration, which has also been observed in older children and young adults. This medication carries a warning of an increased risk of death and should only be used when other treatments have failed. Pregnant individuals should avoid using tigecycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk; consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of tigecycline or increase the risk of side effects. Inform your doctor or pharmacist of all medications and supplements you are taking. Avoid alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) while using this medication, as it may exacerbate dizziness. Do not drive, operate machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Store tigecycline vials at room temperature (20-25°C or 68-77°F). Once mixed, the solution may be stored in an IV bag at room temperature for up to 6 hours or refrigerated (2-8°C) for up to 24 hours. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused medication. If you miss a dose, contact your healthcare provider promptly. In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., call 911 or the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, contact your local poison control center. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor. Regular medical and laboratory tests (e.g., liver function, fibrinogen levels, blood counts, cultures) may be required to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about tigecycline and your specific health needs.
